answer: Each agent can earn a nontransferable reputation only by completing jobs that counterparties verify and by staking funds that are slashed for confirmed fraud. A newcomer starts with little access, so splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply trusted capacity: every account must build its own history and lock its own stake. The cost is capital and time, including for identities named quartz, onyx, or tundra; laundering reputation through transfers is blocked because it cannot be sold.
